steps: Agree the commerce events to collect with your team, and record the IMS org ID and datastream ID for the storefront.
Add the IMS org ID and datastream ID to the storefront configuration, so the storefront sends commerce events to the Experience Platform Edge Network.
Connect your consent management platform, since the boilerplate denies consent by default, and test that events follow each visitor's choice.
Run product views, cart actions and purchases in a test session, check that each event reaches the Edge Network, and record the results.
deliverables: Storefront configuration with organization and datastream
Event test record for product, cart and purchase events
asks: Access to the storefront configuration and its GitHub repository
A contact who owns your consent management platform and its settings
risk: Events that never send because consent is denied by default: we connect your consent platform first and test both consent choices before sign-off.
outcome: Your storefront sends product, cart and purchase events to the Experience Platform Edge Network, in line with each visitor's consent.

steps: Agree with your Commerce and data teams which storefront, back office and profile data to send, and how each flows for your deployment.
Configure the Commerce Services connector first, then finish with the Data Connection extension, in the order Adobe documents.
Create the schema, datasets and datastream in Experience Platform, and turn on storefront, back office and profile data in Data Connection.
Check the first events and records as they arrive in the datasets, and for an Edge Delivery storefront, check events sent through its own settings.
deliverables: Configured Commerce Services connector and Data Connection extension
Schema, datasets and datastream in Experience Platform
Data flow record by data type
asks: Admin access to Adobe Commerce and to Experience Platform for the setup
A decision on which back office and profile data may be sent to Experience Platform
risk: Back office or profile data that takes a different route on your deployment: we agree each data type's path first and test each one before sign-off.
outcome: Your Commerce storefront, back office and profile data reach Experience Platform, ready for Real-Time CDP profiles and audiences.

steps: Agree the first audiences with your marketing team, and how each will be used: a cart price rule, a dynamic block or a related product rule.
Set up the Adobe Commerce destination and Audience Activation, and activate the agreed Real-Time CDP audiences to Commerce.
Build the first cart price rules, dynamic blocks or related product rules on those audiences, with your merchandising team.
Test each rule with a profile that belongs to the audience and one that does not, and record the results.
deliverables: Adobe Commerce destination and Audience Activation setup
First rules and blocks using your audiences
asks: The first audiences to use, and the offers or content each should see
A merchandiser who can approve cart price rules and dynamic blocks
risk: An offer reaching the wrong customers: we test each rule with members and non-members of its audience before it goes live.
outcome: Your Real-Time CDP audiences shape cart offers and on-site content in Commerce, through rules your team can adjust.

steps: Agree the creative groups and the Assets folders each works in, and record users, groups and permissions in an access sheet.
Include the Adobe Asset Link extension in your Creative Cloud deployment packages in the Adobe Admin Console, and deploy them to the creative users.
Add the creative users to the AEM environment's product profile, and grant their groups permissions on the agreed Assets folders.
Test open, check out and save in Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign with a user from each group, and record the results.

Product profile and folder permissions for creative groups
Access sheet of users, groups and folders
asks: An Admin Console administrator to build or approve the deployment packages
The creative users and groups, and the Assets folders each needs
risk: Designers who can see assets but not save back: we test check out and save with each group before rollout.
outcome: Your designers open, check out and save AEM Assets files from a panel inside Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.

steps: Agree with your team which users work in other applications and file types, and where their work in progress should live.
Install and configure the Experience Manager desktop app for those users, with automatic upload turned off where work in progress should not create versions.
Test opening, editing and saving an asset with each group, and give them a one-page guide to the desktop app.
deliverables: Installed and configured Experience Manager desktop app
asks: The users who work in applications outside Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign
Rights to install software on those users' computers
risk: Unfinished files saved as new versions: we turn automatic upload off where needed and show users when to save back.
outcome: Your people who work in other applications reach the same AEM Assets files from their desktop, without unwanted versions.

steps: Agree the working practice with your creative leads: when to check out, where work in progress lives and when to save back to AEM Assets.
Write it up as a short guide for your creatives, including how to relink InDesign layouts to DAM assets.
Teach it in a hands-on session with your creatives, using their own files and Adobe Asset Link.
asks: Creative leads to agree the practice and sign off the guide
Time from your creatives for one hands-on session
risk: Creatives keeping work outside the DAM: we build the practice with your leads and teach it on real files, so it fits their day.
outcome: Your creatives follow one practice for checking out, saving and relinking assets, so AEM Assets holds the current files.

steps: Publish the approved custom models and share them with your design team, with the right permission for each person.
Check with a designer from the team that each model appears and generates in Illustrator.
Walk your designers through prompting and finishing generated images, with a short prompt guide for each model.

A designer's time to test each model in Illustrator
risk: A designer with the wrong permission on a model: we record each person's permission and test with a designer before handover.
outcome: Your designers generate images from your approved custom models inside the Creative Cloud apps they work in.

steps: Agree the fields with your designers, and prepare your InDesign layouts with Data Merge fields for text and images.
Build the data source for each template, with the copy, prices and image references your production workflows fill.
Upload each template with its linked assets and fonts to the Merge InDesign data node, and map the fields to workflow inputs.

asks: The InDesign layouts, with their linked assets and fonts
A designer to agree the fields and approve the proofs

outcome: Your production workflows fill your InDesign templates with copy, prices and images, producing personalized documents at scale in Workflow Builder.

steps: Agree with the designer which text layers, Smart Objects and image layers each Photoshop template should replace.
Tag those layers in each template and upload it to the Merge Photoshop data node, where the tags appear as input ports.

Sample copy and images for proofing
risk: Replacement images or copy that do not fit a layer: we proof real samples with the designer before the workflow runs at scale.
outcome: Your production workflows place copy and images into your Photoshop templates on every run, keeping the designer's layout.

steps: Add Adobe Workfront for design and video to your Creative Cloud deployment packages, or build plugin-only packages, in the Adobe Admin Console.
Deploy the packages to your designers and sign each of them in to the right Workfront domain.

asks: An Admin Console administrator to build or approve the packages

risk: Designers signed in to the wrong Workfront domain: we record the domain in the package plan and check each designer's sign-in.
outcome: Your designers see their Workfront assignments, comments and approvals inside their Creative Cloud apps.

steps: Check that your Workfront projects use Adobe cloud storage, since only those appear in the Projects panel, and list the projects that do not.
Set the document folders designers work from in each project, with your project managers.

A project manager to agree the document folders
risk: A save that changes a document under approval: we show designers what saving does there and agree with your project managers when to save.
outcome: Your designers open, edit and save Workfront project files from the Projects panel in Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.

steps: Agree the CRM objects and fields with your CRM administrator, and the ID they share with your web data, in a mapping record.
Set up the Experience Platform CRM source with an API user, and map each object to a profile, lookup or event schema.

Adobe's IP addresses allowed on your CRM, where it requires them

outcome: Your agreed CRM data loads into Customer Journey Analytics on a schedule, joined to your web data on a shared ID.

steps: Arrange write access with your CRM administrator, since activity sync and opt-out write-back need it, and turn on activity sync.
Agree the CRM Sync Rules with your sales operations team: which lead, contact, account or opportunity fields change at each prospect event.
Set each rule for added, replied, meeting booked, opted out, bounced and finished with no reply, with tokens for the representative, workflow and meeting time.
Test each rule against your CRM validation rules with a test prospect, and record the field changes.
deliverables: CRM Sync Rules for each prospect event
asks: A CRM administrator who can grant write access
Decisions on which status fields change at each prospect event
risk: A rule that your CRM validation rules reject: we test every rule against those rules with a test prospect before go-live.
outcome: Your CRM status fields update as each prospect moves through an Outbound Workflow, so representatives no longer update them by hand.

steps: Install the Marketo Qualifier plugin in your Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365 with your CRM administrator.
Add its components to the Lead, Contact and Account record pages, so representatives see Marketo Sales Insights and AI-generated insights.
Add the Add to Outbound Workflow and Add to Marketo Campaign buttons to Salesforce list views and page layouts.
Test each component and button with a representative's login, and record what each role sees.
deliverables: Components on Lead, Contact and Account record pages
Salesforce buttons on list views and layouts
asks: A CRM administrator who can install the plugin and edit page layouts
A representative's test login for each role
risk: Components that do not show for some representatives: we test with a real representative's login for each role before rollout.
outcome: Your representatives see Marketo Qualifier insights on their CRM record pages, and in Salesforce add prospects to Outbound Workflows and Marketo campaigns.

steps: Agree the attributes to export from the CRM with your team, and line up the customer ID with how the site identifies visitors.
Export the agreed attributes into a file keyed on the customer ID, and create the Customer Attributes source.
Subscribe the source to Target, and set up the file feed, by browser upload or FTP, within Adobe's limits.
Check with a known test visitor that the agreed attributes reach Target on the customer ID, and record the results.
deliverables: Customer Attributes source subscribed to Target
File feed by browser upload or FTP
asks: A CRM contact who can export the agreed attributes on a schedule
How your site identifies signed-in visitors, from your web team
risk: Attributes that never reach visitors because IDs do not match: we line up the customer ID first and test with known visitors.
outcome: Your agreed CRM attributes reach Target on a file feed keyed on the customer ID, ready for your tests and personalized experiences.

steps: Plan the site and root folder with your IT team, and agree whether authors work in SharePoint or Google Drive.
Run Adobe's app registration and site grant with your Microsoft 365 admin, or share the Google Drive folder, and set the site configuration.
Check preview and publish in Sidekick, then train your authors to write, preview and publish pages from Word or Google Docs.
deliverables: Connected SharePoint site or Google Drive folder
asks: A Microsoft 365 admin for the app registration and site grant, or access to share the Google Drive folder
The authors to train, and time for the session
risk: A grant that misses the authors' folder: we agree the root folder first and test preview and publish before training.
outcome: Your authors write pages in Word or Google Docs, preview them and publish them to the site from Sidekick.

steps: Connect Sites Optimizer to your documents: an app registration with a client secret on your SharePoint, or a share on your Google Drive folder.
Check the connection, then deploy one eligible pilot content fix through that opportunity's write-back route, for your authors to review and publish.
Plan the secret's rotation with your IT team, with an owner and a date recorded in your runbook.
deliverables: Sites Optimizer connected to your documents
Pilot content fix in a source document
asks: A SharePoint or Google admin for the app registration or folder share
risk: A lapsed client secret that stops write-back: we agree a rotation plan with a named owner before handover.
outcome: For eligible opportunities, approved Sites Optimizer fixes land in your source documents, ready for your authors to review and publish from Sidekick.

steps: Agree the file feeds, their storage location and format with your data team, and record each field in a mapping record.
Create the schema and dataset, and set up the Experience Platform cloud storage source with its authentication, files, mapping and schedule.
Add each dataset to your CJA connection, and its fields to the data view, with names your analysts agree.
Check the first scheduled loads, and reconcile the records in CJA against the source files for an agreed day.
deliverables: Scheduled dataflows for the agreed feeds
Datasets in the CJA connection and data view
asks: The storage location, credentials and delimited files, or JSON or Parquet files in XDM format
Adobe's IP addresses allowed on the storage, where it requires them
risk: Files that change shape between loads: we agree the format with your data team and test with real files before the schedule starts.
outcome: Your file feeds load into Customer Journey Analytics on a schedule, so their data sits in the same reports as your other channels.

steps: Agree your journey conventions and pre-launch checks with your journey team, and note where Adobe's shipped journey skills already cover them.
Write Skills for your own conventions and checks, on top of Journey Create and the fallout, conflict and anomaly checks, with approval steps.

Hand over each Skill with a short guide to when to use it and who approves its output.
deliverables: Skills for your journey conventions and checks
asks: Your journey conventions and pre-launch checklist, as written today
A journey owner to test the Skills and approve their output
risk: A Skill that repeats or contradicts Adobe's shipped journey skills: we map your checks against them first and build only the gaps.
outcome: Your team builds and checks journeys in Coworker to your own conventions, with an approval step before anything goes live.

steps: Map the Brand Concierge conversation data and its route through Experience Platform, and agree handling and access with your compliance team.
Assemble the approved reference set with your reviewers: current product facts for the products in scope.

Run functional tests on each Skill, produce the reviewer report in the agreed format, and have your reviewers reproduce sampled findings against source conversations.
asks: Named reviewers who check the findings and keep every compliance judgment
Current product references for the products in scope
Approval of how conversation data is handled and accessed
risk: A flagged mismatch taken as a compliance decision: the Skills only flag for review, and your reviewers keep every compliance judgment.
outcome: Your reviewers see conversation themes and flagged answers checked against your approved references, in one report with the evidence linked.

steps: Agree the AI-channel measures and report format with your analytics team, beyond Adobe's executive-summary and KPI-digest skills, and map each to the data view.
Build two Skills: an AI-channel performance readout, and a quality check that flags missing data and unsupported conclusions for human review.
Test each Skill against agreed CJA reports until the outputs reconcile, and record the test evidence.
Hand the Skills to your team with a short guide to running the readout and acting on its flags.
asks: Confirmation of your CJA edition and Coworker access before work starts
An analyst to agree the measures and check the readouts
risk: A readout that disagrees with your reports: each Skill is tested against agreed CJA reports, and the quality check flags gaps for review.
outcome: Your team runs a repeatable AI-channel readout from Customer Journey Analytics in Coworker, checked for missing data before anyone relies on it.

steps: Agree the content-change workflow and brand and quality review with your authors, beyond Adobe's page-update, bulk-update and brand-compliance skills.
Collect the approved brand context, and set permission and review checks so every change goes to your authors before publishing.
Build two Skills, and validate them on agreed pilot pages and templates on your AEM route.
Record test and rollback evidence, and write release guidance for your authors and approvers.
asks: AEM agent access in Coworker for the people who will use the Skills
Authors to approve the brand context and review pilot changes
risk: A change published without review: each Skill sends changes to your authors, and we test access boundaries and rollback on pilot pages first.
outcome: Your authors make approved content changes and brand reviews through Coworker on your AEM site, and review and publish each change.

steps: Write a prompt set with your marketing team for performance summaries, best and worst ads, and drafts from a recommendation.
Test each prompt in Coworker with your team's own sign-ins and permissions, and refine it until its answers match what Insights shows.
Agree who may publish an approved ad from a conversation, and record it in a short publishing rule.
Train the team on the prompt set, from asking how ads are performing to sending a draft for review.
asks: The people who will use the prompts, with their GenStudio permissions
A decision on who may publish from a conversation
risk: An ad published from a conversation without approval: we agree who may publish first and train the team on the review step.
outcome: Your team asks Coworker how ads are performing, assembles drafts from recommendations and sends them for review in one conversation.

steps: Agree your audience conventions and checks with your audience team, and note where Adobe's shipped audience skills already cover them.
Write Skills for your own conventions and checks, on top of the creation, sizing, search and publish skills, with approval steps.
Test each Skill on sample audience requests in Coworker's workspace, and record the results against agreed expected outputs.
Hand over the Skills with a guide naming who approves an audience before it is published.
deliverables: Skills for your audience conventions and checks
asks: Your audience naming conventions and checks, as written today
An audience owner to test the Skills and approve their output
risk: An audience published outside your conventions or data-use rules: each Skill carries your checks and an approval step before publishing.
outcome: Your team creates and checks Real-Time CDP audiences in Coworker to your own conventions, with approval before any audience is published.

steps: Agree the routine Target work to cover, such as test briefs and results summaries, and the formats your team uses today.
Write Skills for that work in your formats, on top of Adobe's shipped Target skills for guided activity setup, with approval steps.
Test each Skill in Coworker Chat, in its own window and inside the Target interface, and record the results.
Hand over the Skills with a guide naming who approves a test brief or a results summary before it is shared.

asks: Examples of your current test briefs and results summaries
A testing lead to try the Skills and approve their output
risk: A results summary that overstates a test: each Skill follows your format and an approval step before anything is shared.
outcome: Your team produces test briefs and results summaries in your own formats through Coworker, with an approval step for each.

steps: Agree the warehouse tables your orchestrated campaigns need with your data team, and record keys and owners in a table inventory.

steps: Agree the tables with your data team, confirm change tracking is on for each one, and record keys and owners in a table inventory.

The list of tables, and the person ID they share with your other data

outcome: Your warehouse tables stay in step with Customer Journey Analytics, updates and deletes included, so reports read current data.

steps: Agree the tables with your data team, with their keys and the person ID they share with your other data, in a table inventory.
Connect the Snowflake, Google BigQuery or Azure Databricks source with your data team, with the allowed IP addresses and access to the agreed tables.
Map each table to a schema, set incremental loading and the schedule, and record the fields in a mapping record.
Check the first load, reconcile record counts against the warehouse, and test that the records join to profiles on the agreed ID.

The list of tables, and the person ID they share with your other data
risk: Records that do not join to your profiles: we agree the shared ID first and test the match on a sample before the scheduled loads.
outcome: Your warehouse tables load into Experience Platform on a schedule, ready for Real-Time CDP profiles and audiences.

Test browsing, placing and saving with a user from each group, and record the results.

Filters and saved searches by channel

steps: Assign Express Enterprise licenses to your Journey Optimizer content creators, so they have the full Adobe Express Web editor.

Template sheet of fields and locks

steps: Check that your Express Enterprise licenses sit in the same IMS organization as Marketo Engage.
